clue.text: Give hunk of American a start in this game

indicators.note: to give a hunk of something is to hand over a chunk cut from inside it, so a run of letters is taken from the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone is told to give a piece of an American a head start in the card game being played.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'AmeriCAN A STArt'; 'this game' is the definition, with 'in' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Canasta is a rummy-style card game played with two packs, so it is a game.

clue.text: Savage and deformed slave keeping a liberal in prison

indicators.note: a prison keeping someone holds them inside, so the jail word wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: can is slang for a prison
Lib is the short form of Liberal, the political party

explanation.surface: A brutal, misshapen slave locks up a liberal in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the description of the servant in the cast list of Shakespeare's The Tempest.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's The Tempest lists its savage, misshapen servant to Prospero by exactly this description in the cast list.

clue.text: Quick sleep and a round of applause after five wins in a row

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep
a big hand is a round of clapping, so hand means applause

explanation.surface: A snooze and some clapping greet a fivefold winning streak.
explanation.walkthrough: In the card game nap, winning all five tricks is the top call; 'after' is only a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase comes from the card game nap, where taking every one of the five tricks scores a full set of consecutive victories.

clue.text: Persevere with criticism

definitions.meaning: to ... at or ... with something is to keep going with it
to take ... is to be on the receiving end of harsh comments

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to keep going in spite of harsh comments.
explanation.definitionFit: Stick (at) means keep going doggedly, and getting stick is British slang for receiving fault-finding.

clue.text: Citadel produces a yield on bad soil

parts.note: a crop is the yield of a harvest

indicators.note: bad soil is spoiled, so its letters are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: A fortress somehow manages a harvest on poor ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' turns SOIL into OLIS; 'produces' and 'on' are only links.
explanation.definitionFit: An acropolis is the fortified upper part of an ancient Greek city, the best known being in Athens, so it is a stronghold.

clue.text: Blundering American gets miserable discharge

parts.note: sad means miserable
to sack is to dismiss or discharge from a job

explanation.surface: A bumbling American is unhappily fired.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is US slang for an inept, hapless person, so it describes a bungling American.

clue.text: You and I in group that's pleasant

indicators.note: the pair of us is placed in the group word, inside its letters

parts.note: a set is a group
you and I together are we

explanation.surface: Being part of a gang together is a nice thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet is a common synonym for pleasant or agreeable.

clue.text: Hide half what Bach did? Rot!

indicators.note: only the second half of the word Hide is kept here

parts.note: Bach composed music, so his activity was to compose

explanation.surface: A cry of 'Rot!' at a puzzling remark about hiding part of what Bach did.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' keeps the back half of HIDE, giving DE; 'Rot' is a verb meaning decay, not an exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: To decompose is to decay, which is what organic matter does when it rots.

clue.text: Single sailor gets seafood

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
alone means single or by oneself

explanation.surface: A lone sailor obtains something to eat from the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The charade is in answer order: the sailor comes before 'Single'.
explanation.definitionFit: Abalone is an edible sea snail, a shellfish eaten as a delicacy.

clue.text: Pets for nervous people?

parts.note: someone very anxious is said to be having young cats, so such animals are the pets of the jittery

explanation.surface: A query about which animals suit anxious owners.
explanation.walkthrough: The British idiom 'having kittens' means being very nervous or agitated.
explanation.definitionFit: Young cats are pets, and the idiom links them to anxiety, so these are pets for the panicky.

clue.text: Cheekier Italian painter meets the Queen

parts.note: Filippo Lippi was a Florentine Renaissance painter
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: An Italian artist becomes rather impudent on meeting the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Lippy is informal for impertinent, so its comparative means more impudent.

clue.text: Captivate, using central part of men's chorus

indicators.note: the central part of a word is what remains between its outer letters

parts.note: a chant is a chorus sung or called out together

explanation.surface: A male choir's central section wins over its audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'central part of' men's gives EN, the letters between M and S.
explanation.definitionFit: To enchant is to charm or bewitch, which is to hold someone spellbound.

clue.text: Fungal disease found in a dangerous place

definitions.meaning: a fungal infection of roses that leaves dark marks on leaves
an accident ... is a stretch of road where crashes often happen

explanation.surface: A plant infection has turned up somewhere hazardous.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a rose leaf blight and a hazardous site where accidents cluster.

clue.text: Deer making animal noises with force

parts.note: moos are the noises cattle make
E is the symbol for electromotive force in physics

explanation.surface: A deer bellows loudly like cattle.
explanation.walkthrough: E for force is a loose convention: it is the physics symbol for electromotive force.
explanation.definitionFit: The moose is the largest member of the deer family, called elk in Britain.

clue.text: Draw attention to end of leg seen in the altogether

indicators.note: the letter is seen inside the word for naked

parts.note: in the altogether means naked, so it gives nude

indicators.note: the end of leg is its final letter

explanation.surface: Pointing out the foot of a leg on someone who is naked.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudge is a gentle prod to remind someone or point something out, so to nudge is to prompt.

clue.text: A lost race, wandering, has its ups and downs

indicators.note: letters that wander roam into a new order

explanation.surface: A race that has been lost, with runners straying, is a mixed affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has its ups and downs' sounds like a remark on the race but describes the answer itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A moving staircase carries people upwards and downwards, so it literally rises and falls.

clue.text: Remains with port on top of sideboard

parts.note: port is the left-hand side of a ship
on and over both mean resting above

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Remnants of a meal sit with a decanter of port on the sideboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' is the ship's left side, not the drink the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Leftovers are remains of a meal, food not eaten and kept for later.

clue.text: Rapid route for diet course

parts.note: to fast is to go without food, an extreme diet
a track is a course for racing

explanation.surface: A quick way to the goal for a slimming plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast track is a quicker way to achieve something, a speedy path to a goal.

clue.text: Displays what Latin teacher may do to class

definitions.meaning: exhibits or presents things to view

definitions.text: what Latin teacher may do to class
definitions.meaning: a Latin teacher demonstrates the grammatical cases of nouns to pupils

explanation.surface: A teacher of Latin shows the class some examples.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits as SHOW CASES: Latin nouns decline through cases such as nominative and accusative.
explanation.definitionFit: To showcase is to exhibit to best advantage, so the verb means displays.

clue.text: Swimmer with the deep voice?

parts.note: the deep is a poetic name for the sea
bass is the lowest male singing voice

explanation.surface: A fish with a low-pitched singing voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deep voice' suggests a bass singer, but 'the deep' is the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea bass is a fish, and fish are swimmers.

clue.text: This is about departure in progress

parts.note: on means about, as in a talk on a subject
going is leaving or departure

explanation.surface: A remark that a leaving is currently under way.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ongoing is continuing or still happening, that is, under way.

clue.text: Short announcer says: "Get me back to the church on time, eventually!"

indicators.note: getting me back means writing it the other way round

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: eventually points to the last letter, what comes at the end

explanation.surface: A compere asks to be returned to the wedding in good time, in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short announcer' is MC, master of ceremonies, spelt out; the surface echoes the song 'Get Me to the Church on Time'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the spelt-out form of MC, master of ceremonies, the person who introduces acts.

clue.text: Almost stylish, certainly not in favour of wine

indicators.note: almost the whole word, with its final letter cut off

parts.note: chic means stylish
anti means against, firmly not in favour of

explanation.surface: Someone nearly fashionable who is firmly opposed to wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red wine from Tuscany in Italy.

clue.text: I, reportedly, stroke hair

indicators.note: reportedly signals a word that sounds like the one given

parts.note: the letter I is pronounced like the organ of sight
a lash is a stroke of a whip

explanation.surface: Someone says they stroke their hair.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a single hair growing on the edge of the eyelid.

clue.text: Have some American cake, darling

definitions.meaning: ... food cake is a light American sponge
an affectionate term for a beloved person

explanation.surface: An offer of a slice of American cake, darling.
explanation.definitionFit: Angel food cake is an American sponge, and angel is a term of endearment for a sweetheart.

clue.text: "Listen to the band" is a slogan

parts.note: to catch a performance is to go and hear it
a line is a band or stripe

explanation.surface: An exhortation to hear the group, used as a catchphrase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' looks like a music group but is a stripe.
explanation.definitionFit: A catchline is a catchy phrase used in advertising, a type of slogan.

clue.text: Made better with copper colour

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
red is a colour

explanation.surface: Something improved by a copper hue.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cured is to be restored to health, healed of an illness.

clue.text: Rodent found in shed in Austria, originally

parts.note: a hut is a shed

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A rodent discovered in an Austrian outbuilding.
explanation.definitionFit: The hutia is a large rodent native to the Caribbean islands.

clue.text: High-flyer takes one through rocky place

parts.note: a means one
via means by way of or through
a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor in England

explanation.surface: An ambitious achiever takes a route over a crag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-flyer' suggests a go-getter, but here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot flies high in the sky, so a high-flyer taken literally is one.

clue.text: Girl one way or another holds back material for the aerial

indicators.note: the girl's name holds the other piece within it
the name reads the same in either direction

parts.note: Anna is a girl's name

indicators.note: back means the word for the material is turned round

parts.note: net is a mesh material

explanation.surface: A girl wraps up some fabric to use on a radio aerial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' makes TEN, which goes in the middle of a girl's name that reads the same both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: An antenna is a rod or wire receiving radio signals, also called an aerial.

clue.text: Sweet Sue needing drag, perhaps?

indicators.note: perhaps hints that these letters are one possible arrangement among others

explanation.surface: Lovely Sue may need to dress in drag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet Sue' reads like a name, but 'Sweet' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugared food has been coated with sugar, so it is sweetened.

clue.text: Wicked king has his van repaired

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: something repaired is put back together, so its letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A villainous king gets his vehicle fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: A knave is a rogue, so knavish means dishonest or roguish.
